name: Cover the largest disk with 21 unit disks
definition: Choose the centers of 21 unit disks in the plane so their union covers a closed disk centered at the origin. Maximize the target disk radius.
solution_format: An object with positive rational radius and exactly 21 centers [[x,y]]. Coordinates and radius are exact rational strings or integers. Repeated centers are allowed.
constraints: There are exactly 21 circles of radius 1.
The target is the closed disk centered at (0,0) with the submitted positive rational radius.
Circle centers may be any rational coordinates; there is no coordinate range or denominator cap.
Every point of the target disk must lie in at least one covering disk.

The rational-coordinate and rational-radius domain has the same supremum as the unrestricted real domain: contract all centers and the target disk by a rational factor below 1 to create coverage slack, approximate the centers by rationals, and choose a rational target radius approaching the original radius.
verification: The checker proves continuous coverage by exactly enumerating restricted Voronoi vertices, circle-boundary bisector intersections, boundary distance extrema, and fixed representatives. Every candidate coverage test uses exact rational or quadratic-field arithmetic; there is no sampling.

source_review.definition: Exactly21 unit disks, arbitrary unbounded rational centers, maximize positive rational radius of a concentric covered disk. Duplicate centers allowed. Contracting centers and target, then rational approximation, preserves the continuous supremum.
source_review.human_source: Classical Kershner1939 triangular lattice covering method, finite19-site hexagonal patch with2 repeated origins. This local finite-method reconstruction covers7/2; it is not claimed as a separately published21-circle score. Tan2018 reported radius3.804 remains an unreproduced best public value in reviewed Friedman sources.
source_review.independent_method: Root proves ideal scaled triangular tessellation covers the plane with radius999/1000; every omitted site has norm>=scale*sqrt21>7/2+1, so covering sites for the target are retained. Exact rational sqrt3 perturbation error<10^-60 gives retained-center displacement<=2scale*10^-60 and total covering radius<1. Root checks witness equality to this finite formula. Cold/search constructions contain an origin unit disk and haveR1. Formal checker instead enumerates restricted Voronoi vertices and boundary extrema.
source_review.audit_scope: Independent analytic audit covers these admission constructions; other search structures require a separate independent proof before promotion. Formal verifier accepts general rational center layouts and performs full-domain checking.
